prompt: Let $A$ be a set and $R\subseteq A\times A$ a binary relation on $A$. For $x,y\in A$, write $R(x,y)$ for $(x,y)\in R$. Which property is defined exactly by $\forall x\in A\;\forall y\in A\; ((R(x,y)\land R(y,x))\Rightarrow x=y)$?

answers.explanation: Mutual relatedness forces equality. Self-loops are allowed.
Every related pair has its reverse; loops are allowed but not required. That is a different condition from the displayed formula.
Every element has a self-loop; pairs of different elements are unrestricted. That is a different condition from the displayed formula.
Every two-step chain has its direct shortcut, including chains with repeated vertices. That is a different condition from the displayed formula.
Every related pair has no reverse. Taking the two elements equal also forbids loops. That is a different condition from the displayed formula.
No element has a self-loop; pairs of different elements are unrestricted. That is a different condition from the displayed formula.
Some related pair lacks its reverse; this is an existential violation. That is a different condition from the displayed formula.
Every related pair is diagonal; some or all loops may be missing. That is a different condition from the displayed formula.
An element has at most one outgoing related element; it need not have any. That is a different condition from the displayed formula.
All diagonal pairs and no off-diagonal pairs are present. That is a different condition from the displayed formula.
